summary: Iteration 18 — Per-interval target-vs-actual compliance in Summary + AI debrief. Backend 3/3 pytest PASSED (/app/backend/tests/test_intervals_debrief.py): POST /api/coach/debrief accepts the new 'interval_compliance' and 'intervals' fields and returns a pacing-aware debrief (200) referencing wattage and effort; still backward-compatible when those fields are omitted; POST /api/workouts/summarize regression OK. Frontend (landscape tablet 1280x800) — full ride → summary flow verified end-to-end: opened /workout?workoutId=vo2-max-intervals (loaded with VO2 Max, target 187 W, STEP 1/13), let telemetry stream ~14 s, clicked bottom 'END WORKOUT' → router.replace('/summary'). On /summary the INTERVAL TARGETS card (testID interval-targets-card) rendered with REAL scores (no dashes): TARGET ACCURACY 6% in header, subtitle 'Your power vs each segment's target'. Per-row TARGET watts match zone×FTP@287 spec exactly — Warm-up Z2 187 W, Tempo Block Z3 230 W, Z4 Efforts 273 W, Z5 Efforts 321 W, Recovery/Cool-down Z1 144 W. YOURS column shows real avg watts (Warm-up 207 W → 75% accuracy; subsequent efforts scored 0% because a 14-second ride only fills the warm-up slice — expected, since ride recorder samples cluster near the first segment's target). Alberto's recap explicitly referenced per-interval performance: 'That warm-up at 207 watts showed me you have real engine…' and 'hitting only 187 watts when I needed 321 on those Z5 efforts tells me you are not trusting the discomfort yet…' — proves the intervals payload reaches the LLM and shapes the recap. Regression: /workout?workoutId=endurance-ride still shows different STEP count vs vo2-max-intervals (verified in iteration_17, unchanged in this iteration). Direct-open /summary fallback (planned targets + dashes + subtitle 'Planned targets for this session — ride it to score your accuracy') already confirmed working by main agent.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warnings on /workout still present: 'textShadow*' style props are deprecated (use 'textShadow' object) and props.pointerEvents is deprecated (use style.pointerEvents). Non-blocking. Reference: /app/frontend/app/workout.tsx and /app/frontend/src/components/workout.tsx

action_items: None blocking. Optional (carry-over from iter 17): migrate deprecated 'textShadow*' and props.pointerEvents on /workout to silence RN Web console warnings.

Optional UX: consider showing a small 'partial ride' hint on the interval card when the recorded sample duration covers only the first few segments (currently unmeasured segments still display avgW because the proportional slice picks up warm-up samples — accurate to spec but could confuse a rider who quit after 14s).
critical_code_review_comments: summary.ts computeIntervals() proportionally slices recorded samples across segments by cumulative duration ratio. That is correct for a full ride but on a very short ride every segment gets some warm-up samples — reflected in the observed avgW ~185W on downstream Z3/Z4/Z5 rows and 0% accuracy. Behaviour matches design; note if you ever want 'unmeasured' semantics you'd need per-segment timing metadata on samples.

summary.ts useCoachDebrief() slices 'measured' intervals to first 10 and only sends segments with avgW != null and targetW > 0 — keeps prompt tight. Confirmed the LLM cited specific segments (warm-up 207 W, Z5 needed 321 W).

server.py CoachDebriefRequest declares interval_compliance and intervals with sensible defaults (0 and []), so old clients continue to work — verified via test_debrief_backwards_compat_without_intervals.
server.py coach_debrief builds intervals_txt only when req.intervals is non-empty, and the overall interval_compliance is included in the prompt — good.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows (ride→summary scored intervals verified end-to-end; regression on distinct workout STEP counts holds)

seed_data_creation: None. Debrief tests use transient payloads; the ride→summary flow persists a ride_history row via /workouts/summarize as before.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The end-to-end ride→summary path is fully functional as of iteration 18. To reproduce: 1) mobile viewport 1280x800; 2) goto /workout?workoutId=<id>; 3) wait 12–15 s (do NOT reload); 4) click bottom 'END WORKOUT' (green text at bottom-right, no dedicated testID — used page.get_by_text('END WORKOUT') successfully); 5) /summary card 'interval-targets-card' will show real YOURS watts and TARGET ACCURACY %. Backend debrief tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_intervals_debrief.py. If EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is unset the debrief endpoint returns 503 — acceptable per problem statement.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. Note for design: the compliance % for segments beyond the actual recorded ride duration will always be low because the module-level ride recorder samples get proportionally split across the full planned timeline. This is by design; a fully completed ride will populate every segment slice with real telemetry.
